notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is "unavailable" in per_rule. The runs were made at 58f6318 with the uncommitted rule changes (result.json uncommitted: true, skill_hash 9faec678...).

Newly listed rule for this case, graded against the current text: Chain fallible steps with `with`. The one-step sentence decides the verdict: "With one step there is nothing to chain, and a `with` makes the reader look for the other steps. Use `case`, which shows both outcomes in one place:" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function). The 93873be text already ended its first paragraph with "Use `case` when there is only one step."; the change adds the reason and an example. The else sentences are unchanged.

`with`, violating runs out of four per sentence: one-step with: 1 of 4 (sonnet-2 line 114, in total/2). Large else block: 0 of 4 (no run wrote an else). In the previous sweep the same four tiers' runs had one-step with blocks in 3 of 4 (skill-haiku-2 line 50; skill-sonnet-1 lines 73 and 99; skill-sonnet-2 lines 74 and 98), recorded under other_violations because the rule was not listed for this case then.

The new one-step example in SKILL.md is this case's own apply-code step: `with {:ok, discount} <- parse_discount(code), do: {:ok, apply_discount(cart, discount)}`. All four runs now write that step as a case, while the one remaining one-step with (sonnet-2) is in the total function, which the example does not show. Part of the drop may come from the example matching the prompt rather than from the rule being understood; a case whose step differs from the example would separate the two.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming. The fetch sentence adds "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." and the generic-name sentence adds "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## Naming). Neither addition decides a verdict here.

Naming, violating runs out of four per sentence: CamelCase/snake_case 0 of 4; top-level namespace 0 of 4; boolean functions end in ? 0 of 4 (no run defines a boolean function); get/fetch/fetch! including the new fetch sentence 0 of 4 (no run defines a get or fetch function; the Sonnet runs' subtotal/2, which looks up prices and returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}}, is named by its job); size/length 0 of 4 (not exercised); descriptive names for ignored values 0 of 4 (_held, _reason, _other, _unknown, _code, _discount, _subtotal, _sku); generic variable names 0 of 4 (no data, item, res or x; sonnet-2's sum accumulator was not counted, as the previous sweep did not count it).
